result.title: Where Should a Gate Look? Input vs. State Gating in Diagonal State Space Models
result.summary: Modern state-space models owe much of their computational efficiency to their linear, often diagonal, dynamics. Classical recurrent neural networks instead allow nonlinear state-to-state interactions, which can be beneficial when memory updates need to depend on the past context. In this paper, we ask whether state feedback through a simple gate regulating memory updates can enhance the expressivity of diagonal state-space models. To investigate this question, we compare gates that depend on the current input, the recurrent state, or both. We establish a strict expressivity separation: for scalar models, state gating solves induction-head tasks for arbitrary vocabulary size and sequence length, whereas input gating fails on a finite instance under standard stability assumptions on the state transition matrix. Experiments show that state gating retains its advantage on induction-head tasks in higher-dimensional models, whereas input gating performs better on selective copying tasks. Together, our results show that even a simple, diagonal form of state-feedback gating can unlock capabilities unavailable to input-controlled models, while input and state gating offer complementary strengths and achieve the strongest overall performance when combined.

AI.brief_summary: 该论文比较对角状态空间模型中门控信号取自当前输入、循环状态或两者，从理论上给出严格表达力分离（标量模型下状态门控可解任意词表与长度的 induction-head 任务，输入门控在稳定性假设下失败），并在高维模型上验证，发现二者在 induction-head 与 selective copying 上各有优势、组合最佳。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「输入门控 vs 状态门控」的表达力分析可为循环式 latent 推理中状态更新是否依赖上一步 latent（而非仅依赖输入）提供可核查的理论线索，induction-head 的失败边界也可能对应多步推理中的信息复制与保持问题。
